verdictStatement: Three of the five claimed repairs land cleanly. EXACT-BUILD now carries a named identifierScheme drawn from a closed two-entry map with explicit normalization and a versioned comparison-algorithm identifier; CLOSED-RANGE is prohibited outright as a required-member value until this contract versions a total order, which takes the stronger of the two branches Codex offered; and /platformProfile/slice1ProfileStems is on the v5 roster, which places the previously-unrostered ownerArtifact state inside the rostered re-read surface and makes v5's own closure sentence true — 78 changed leaves, 0 uncovered. What does not land is the filesystem member. The escape gained a tag name, an algorithm identifier and a digest length, but the thing being hashed is named only as 'the UTF-8 NFC filesystem-type token' with no vocabulary, source or case rule, and the repair deleted v4's condition restricting the escape to types outside the enum without replacing it. A required member of the profile key that gates allowlist freeze therefore still cannot be computed identically by two conforming parties, which is the property Codex's blocker was about. The SONAME-ABI repair likewise takes neither branch Codex offered: it is now correctly disqualified as identity and as a fifth field, but no libc authenticity payload defines the optional subfield it says it lives inside, so the companion remains unencodable. Separately, an unchanged governingSources note routes the live coordinator digest to reMeasurementAtV2, which has carried a superseded value since v3.

blockers.title: The filesystem member is still not reproducible: the hashed token is undefined, the escape's applicability condition was deleted, and the member has no serialization rule

measurement.undefinedHashedInput: otherTag.digestEncoding reads '64 lowercase hex characters of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 NFC filesystem-type token'. The token itself is defined nowhere. I searched the whole artifact: 'filesystem-type token' occurs once, in that sentence, and no vocabulary, publishing source, case rule, or example is given anywhere in v5. Two conforming parties describing the same volume can hash 'zfs', 'ZFS', 'openzfs' or a mount-reported string and produce four unequal members, all conforming.
measurement.deletedApplicabilityCondition: v4 read otherForm: 'other:<digest-bound-fstype-token> when the platform publishes a type outside the enum'. v5 removes otherForm and adds otherTag, and the qualifying clause is gone — the string 'outside the enum' occurs zero times in v5. Nothing now restricts OTHER-FSTYPE to types absent from identifierEnum, so apfs has two lawful encodings, the bare enum member and OTHER-FSTYPE over the token 'apfs', which the stated equality makes unequal to each other ('enum members compare byte-exact; OTHER-FSTYPE compares algorithmId plus digest').
measurement.noSerializationRule: The version selector gained an explicit serialization line in this same edit ('exactly one lawful tag object'). The filesystem member gained none, while its form was retitled 'closed tagged identifier' — yet its enum branch is a bare string and its escape branch is a tagged object. Which shapes are lawful, and in what encoding, is unstated.

blockers.whyThisIsTheSameDefectCodexBlocked: PTCB-V4-B1's third evidence bullet was that the escape 'defines no tagged structure, digest algorithm identifier, encoding, length, or validation rule', with the impact that 'the same range endpoints or filesystem escape can compare differently across verifiers' and 'a frozen allowlist and its G22 matrix therefore remain non-deterministic even though all required members are present'. v5 supplies the structure, algorithm identifier, encoding and length. It supplies no validation rule, and the cross-verifier comparison hazard the impact named survives intact for every filesystem outside the six-member enum.
blockers.falseSelfDescription: form claims 'closed tagged identifier owned by this contract' and populationPacket claims 'This contract authors the grammar, including version/build and filesystem selectors'. Both are falsified for the escape branch: the token vocabulary that decides equality is authored nowhere, and the packet is confined to choosing values, so no party is authorized to supply it.
blockers.consequence: Fail-closed rather than exploitable — mismatched encodings refuse rather than substitute — but a required member that two parties cannot compute alike cannot satisfy beforeAllowlistFreeze's 'Every required member MUST be populated' in any way that survives a second verifier.
blockers.requiredRepair: Name the token: give OTHER-FSTYPE a stated source (for example the platform-reported filesystem-type string as a named interface publishes it), a case rule alongside the existing NFC rule, and restore an explicit condition that OTHER-FSTYPE is lawful only for types absent from identifierEnum. Add a serialization rule for the member naming the lawful shapes, as supportedVersionOrBuildSelector already has. Alternatively remove the escape and hold non-enum filesystems out of scope, which Codex also offered.

shouldFix.title: SONAME-ABI is declared to live inside a libc authenticity payload that defines no such subfield, so the companion is still unencodable

measurement.whatChanged: role moves from 'additionalCompatibilitySelector' to 'optionalCompanionInsideLibcAuthenticityPayload'; notASignedEntryField: true and notAuthenticity: true are added; requires becomes 'exact soname plus ABI selector as additional compatibility labels inside a PLATFORM-ATTESTED or DIGEST-BOUND libc payload'; comparison becomes 'companion labels never decide identity'.
measurement.whatDidNot: PLATFORM-ATTESTED.requires and DIGEST-BOUND.requires are byte-identical to v4 and are prose sentences with no field structure at all. Neither declares an optional companion slot, a field name, a grammar for the soname or ABI selector, or that the payload admits additional fields. Codex's exact evidence — 'no authenticity-tag payload defines a SONAME-ABI subfield' — is still literally true at v5.
measurement.neitherOfferedBranchTaken: PTCB-V4-S1 offered exactly two repairs: remove SONAME-ABI and its companion language entirely, or define it as a closed optional subfield inside the permitted libc authenticity-evidence payload with explicit non-identity comparison semantics. v5 supplies the non-identity comparison semantics and keeps the companion language, but defines no subfield, so it lands between the two.
measurement.unionTyping: identityRuleShape.identityEvidence.form says every signed entry carries exactly one tag from the classMap for its class. SONAME-ABI sits inside identityEvidenceUnion.tags but in no classMap list, so 'tags' is not the set of lawful identity tags it presents itself as — it is two identity tags plus one non-identity annotation, inside a structure the contract calls a union.

shouldFix.whatImproved: The determinism harm Codex named is materially reduced, and I record that in fairness. Two of the three divergent producer behaviours he predicted are now explicitly closed: notASignedEntryField: true forbids the fifth-field route, and absence from classMap plus notAuthenticity: true forbids smuggling it as the one identity tag. Only 'drop it' remains conforming, so producers now converge. What is left is a clause describing an optional companion that no conforming artifact can carry.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Either delete SONAME-ABI and its companion language from identityEvidenceUnion and from comparison, or give the libc PLATFORM-ATTESTED and DIGEST-BOUND payloads a named optional subfield with a closed shape for the soname and ABI selector. Do not leave a described-but-unrepresentable option in a contract whose stated purpose is a closed emitted schema.

advisories.title: identifierScheme is not bound to osFamily, and linux-uname-release does not separate publishers
advisories.detail: EXACT-BUILD.requires reads 'identifierScheme from identifierSchemes' with no rule tying macos-product-build to osFamily=macos or linux-uname-release to osFamily=linux, so a profile keyed osFamily=linux carrying a macos-product-build scheme is conforming though meaningless. Separately, a uname -r release string does not identify a distribution or publisher, so two materially different Linux platforms shipping the same kernel release map to one profile key — the collision half of PTCB-V4-B1's impact paragraph.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: Neither costs reproducibility: equality is byte-exact within a named scheme, so two verifiers still agree, and a collision degrades to a member-digest mismatch and a refusal rather than a substitution. Codex's remedy also offered identifierScheme or a publisher-or-variant discriminator as alternatives, and v5 took the first.
advisories.suggestedFix: Add a one-line map from osFamily to its permitted identifierScheme, and note explicitly that a kernel release is not a distribution identity so profile keys are not distribution-distinguishing.

coordinatorNote: v5 is a real advance on v4 and two of its repairs are unusually clean — prohibiting CLOSED-RANGE outright rather than patching an order it cannot supply is the stronger of the two branches Codex offered, and the identifierScheme map plus versioned comparison algorithm answers the version half of PTCB-V4-B1 on its own terms. My own CLAUDE-V4-S1 is closed, and closed correctly: the stems are unchanged, so the fix is purely that a roster-bounded re-read now reaches them. But the same edit that tightened the version selector loosened the filesystem one. It deleted v4's 'when the platform publishes a type outside the enum' condition without replacing it, gave the escape no serialization rule while giving the version selector one, and left the hashed input named only as 'the filesystem-type token' — so a required member of the profile key still cannot be computed identically by two parties, which is exactly what Codex's blocker was about and what his 'validation rule' clause asked for. The SONAME-ABI repair improves producer convergence but takes neither branch he offered; a contract about closed emitted schemas should not describe an option no conforming artifact can carry. I also report a miss of my own: the governingSources note routing the live coordinator digest to reMeasurementAtV2 has been false since v3 and I did not catch it when I reviewed v4 — it is unchanged text, so it breaks no roster claim, but it is false at v5's live bytes and I have graded it S-2 rather than let a prior omission set the bar. DR-126 stays OPEN. No per-OS table is populated, D-096 appears nowhere, nothing here marks the row SATISFIED, qualifies G22, or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/. The subject, file 08 and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md were not edited and nothing was committed.
